items.q: Which steps does Ana follow for the weekly freight accrual?
items.gold: Get the TMS report, match in FBL1N, post with FB50 to G/L 4711000, and set the reversal for the 1st of the month.
items.answer:
Ana Novak's weekly freight accrual (run on Fridays) follows these steps:

- **Get the report:** Tom Hendriks sends the TMS report of delivered-not-invoiced shipments, filtered on actual POD date up to the cut-off, due by 12:00 on the cut-off day. Do not use the planned-date default. It must list shipment, delivery, carrier, site and agreed freight amount [1][2].
- **Match:** Ana matches each line against open items in FBL1N and drops shipments whose invoice is already booked [1].
- **Post:** She posts the remaining total with FB50 to G/L 4711000 [1][2].
- **Set reversal:** The reversal date is the 1st of the following month, so costs aren't counted twice [1][2].
- **Record:** She records the accounting document number in the thread [1].

The last Friday of the month is the month-end close.

judge.reason: The answer covers all reference steps: TMS report, matching in FBL1N, posting with FB50 to G/L 4711000, and the reversal on the 1st of the following month. Every claim matches the cited wiki and email sources.

items.q: When does the new ADR dispatcher check rule start and where is it recorded?
items.gold: From Monday 12 Oct, in a checklist in the WMS.
items.answer:
The dispatcher check started on **Monday 12 Oct 2026**. Marta Kowalska agreed to it on 8 Oct 2026 [7], and Sofie Peeters confirmed the checklist was live in the WMS and dispatchers were briefed on 12 Oct [8].

**Where it is recorded:** in a five-item checklist in the **WMS**, which is a mandatory step in the ADR loading task [1][2]. All five items must be ticked before the task can be closed:
- DGD printed and signed
- UN number and quantity match the delivery
- Packing group stated
- Driver ADR certificate valid

The gate check was proposed but is not decided, so it is not a rule yet [1][3].
